q1: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT(ARTICLE_ID)) >= 2
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT(ARTICLE_ID)) >= 2
counterexample: INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 201, '2023-01-01'); INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 201, '2023-01-02');
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because they group by different columns and have different conditions in the HAVING clause.
counterexample_dsp: Q1 groups by VIEW_DATE and VIEWER_ID, while Q2 groups by VIEWER_ID and VIEW_DATE. The condition in Q1 is COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1, and in Q2, it is COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) >= 2. A counterexample can be created where a viewer views the same article on two different dates, satisfying Q2 but not Q1.
